# Issue #2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
Opened by SergeyBarskiyTyler, 2026-09-11. State: open.

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage
attribute. Writing good coverage for generated MessagePack code is very hard,
which may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of
generated code.

## Describe the solution you'd like
I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage
attribute. I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to
have too.

## Describe alternatives you've considered
There are no alternatives. Good coverage of generated code is close to
impossible because it covers many edge cases.

## Additional context
N/A

## Comments
1. b-kurczynski-dl (2026-10-20): same issue; suggests excluding generated files
   in dotnet-coverage settings via a Sources/Exclude regex `obj\.*\.g\.cs$`.
2. armadavalor (2026-10-25): offers a PR adding
   [global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] and
   possibly [global::System.CodeDom.Compiler.GeneratedCode(...)] to types
   emitted by templates under src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/
   (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), with
   updated verified snapshots. "No setting." Asks AArnott for a decision.
   No maintainer reply on the page.

--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -1636,6 +1636,9 @@ Two assembly-level attributes exist to help with mixing in your own custom forma
 
 Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).
 
+All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so generated code does not skew code coverage reports.
+The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework).
+
 ### MagicOnion
 
 [MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
